anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer chooses a markedly sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are adequate.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly: Overall engine memory consumption grows beyond the safe capacity of the host, triggering OS or engine-level memory pressure.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly: Sessions serialize on hot buffer pages and their associated latches, stalling on low-level synchronization primitives.

When all three anomalies surface together, operators observe a volatile mix of plan instability, memory stress, and internal buffer contention. A single statement may oscillate between index probes and full scans; after each plan flip, rows flood the buffer cache, inflating working-set size, evicting other pages, and expanding per-query work areas. Resident-set bloat pushes the host into paging or swap storms, while the shrinking effective cache intensifies latch waits on the remaining hot pages. Execution latency becomes highly jittery: some executions terminate quickly, others stall on page-latch or memory-pressure waits, and overall throughput collapses with CPUs either spin-locking or blocked by the OS memory manager.

Causal chain: poor plan selection can inflate I/O and memory demand (e.g., hash joins that spill or table scans that load large objects), accelerating buffer-pool turnover and forcing the engine to allocate additional work memory. The enlarged footprint worsens host memory pressure, provoking aggressive page evictions and dirty-page flush cycles. These churns create a handful of survivor pages that every session must repeatedly acquire, amplifying latch competition. Conversely, severe latch contention extends query runtimes, keeping sub-optimal plans resident longer and holding work areas open, which further inflates memory usage. The feedback loop between plan mis-choice, memory exhaustion, and hot-page serialization drives the database into a degraded state that is deeper than any of the single anomalies would have caused on their own.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
